the ratios of branching fractions of the light stop to chargino and neutralino modes can provide a good handle on the stop mixing angle $\theta_{\tilde{t}}$, its CP-violating mixing angle $\phi_{\tilde t}$ and the light stop mass.

, in general, the LHC will not allow to measure the mixing angle and CP phase of the stop sector, but there are some special cases where this may be possible.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the light stop mass and the mixing angle can be measured at the LHC, but the CP phase will be very hard to extract.
a measurement of the stop mixing angle, and possibly the phase, is possible at the LHC in combination with a linear collider.
the stop mixing angle is a parameter which is not only important in the context of electroweak symmetry breaking, but also in the context of CP violation in the stop sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, if the stop is light enough and if the stop mixing angle is sufficiently large, the stop sector will provide a rich phenomenology at the LHC.
the mixing angle can be extracted with a good accuracy at the LHC, even in the presence of large CP-violation in the stop sector.
the stop sector is a rich and promising playground for the LHC and the linear collider, and that the LHC can provide important input for the study of the stop sector at the linear collider.
